pulls.title: Lead with the federation model: thesis, gaps, scope, and WAG status
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Resolves two external reviews of the September draft: (R1) an end-to-end review of the whole draft and (R2) a review of its positioning against enterprise agent-governance reference architectures. Both reviews find the model settled and ask that it lead the document, so this round is framing only.

**No normative change.** The body has 293 BCP 14 sentences before and after, and none was added, removed, or reworded (`normative_diff`). The build, citations, and artwork widths all pass, and the idnits output matches main. The body grows by about 380 words; the page count is unchanged at 113.

Section numbers are the rendered ones.

## Applied

| Commit | Review items | Change |
|---|---|---|
| bb57cdb | R1.2, R2.10 | §1 now lists three gaps existing OAuth leaves open, each with its extension point (ATTEST/SPIFFE-OAUTH, ID-JAG §9.7, RFC 8693 `act`). The AIMS paragraph now positions the draft as a protocol profile, not a governance framework, and two restating paragraphs are gone. |
| a75a93e | R1.1, R2.3, R2 headline invariants | §1 states the governing principle before the relationships table: the Agent Principal is the authorization identity, and client and workload identities are inputs that resolve to it. Three consequences follow: identity is independent of the runtime, resolution is not authorization to use, and actor attribution is not delegation authority. Two sentences that restated this are removed. |
| 1d9eb04 | R1.10, R1 scope note, R2.6 | The scope and exclusions move to the end of §1, adding task or mission authorization and asynchronous approval. The IdP-governed-namespace boundary moves there from §3. Each now appears in one place. |
| 6147467 | R2.5, R2.1 | The Abstract names Identity Binding and Client Association and says the principal persists across platforms and credential rotation. |
| 9418d5c | R1 diagram, R2.9 | §3 has a whole-model figure: evidence, Identity Binding, Agent Principal, Client Association, Delegation or Agent Authorization, grant, RAS correlation, resource authorization. It replaces the namespace figure, which the §4.4 example already covers. |
| 1ed26a8 | R1.4, R2.2 | §3 has a new table separating workload, OAuth client, and Agent Principal by the question each answers. They can coincide in a deployment, but none is inferred from another, and the workload-to-agent relationship need not be one-to-one. |
| f20fada | R1.8, R2.4 | §3.4: actors needing independent governance get distinct principals even when they share a runtime, client, credential, or deployment. An execution that shares all of its governance with an agent, such as an inheriting sub-agent, can run as that agent. |
| 062d97e | R1.5 | WAG is marked as proposed throughout: the Abstract, the §1 layer bullets, the §4.1 table, the implementer table, and the §10 heading ("Proposed Self-Acting WAG Realization"), which now opens with the proposal statement. |
| 90cade4 | R1.3 (rename) | §4.3 becomes "Federation Configuration", and the client-registration bullet cites ID-JAG §5. |
| edce340 | R1.9 | Target Tenant is defined as where authority is exercised, which can differ from the Governance Tenant. |
| db24387 | R1.7 | §8.5.5 now opens with the principle that the component exercising a credential holds its proof key. A duplicate sentence is removed. |
| 9fb160c | all of §1 | The README carries the governing principle, its three consequences, the scope boundary, and WAG's "proposed" status. |
| 76e26fa | family naming | The SCIM management companion is retitled "SCIM Profile for Governed Agent Federation Management", including its reference entries in the other three drafts. |

## Not applied as proposed

- **R1.3, a separate subsection for client-registration mapping.** ID-JAG §5 already requires it: the IdP maintains "a record of each client_id used between Clients and Resource Authorization Servers, which will need to be obtained by out-of-band mechanisms." This round cites that section instead of adding a subsection.
- **R1.8 and R2.3/R2.4 as MUST NOT.** Whether two executions "require independent governance" is an identity-design decision that no counterparty can observe, so these are stated without BCP 14. The observable rule already exists in §3.4: the binding "MUST distinguish exactly one Agent Principal for each authorization transaction".
- **R2.7, actor lineage as a new MUST.** §7.4 already says: "A valid signature or an `act` claim alone does not open the gate; failure to establish it MUST result in denial." It is surfaced as principle 3 in §1, not restated.
- **R1.10, putting the exclusions under Scope.** They were already in §4.2; the problem was placement, which 1d9eb04 fixes.

## Deferred

- **R1.6, protocol surface.** The access-token mode table and the mutual-TLS-with-bound-grant rule are specific to this profile. Candidates such as the §8.5.4 closing restatement of RFC 9449/8705 go to a separate consolidation round with an obligation map.
- **R2.6, the layering and portfolio map (Mission, AuthZEN, and others).** This belongs in the README or WG discussion.
- **R2.8, lifecycle as identity state.** §11.6 already separates execution termination from Agent Principal disablement; anything further goes to the lifecycle companion.
- **R2, citing the Blueprint whitepaper.** The substance lands without a citation. Adding one is a positioning call that needs a stable URL.

pulls.title: Companion architecture: policy-gated JIT correlation, revocation boundaries, family model
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Resolves a review of the two companion drafts, read together with Federation: the SCIM management draft (M) and the lifecycle draft (L). The review also suggested a family architecture.

**Normative change: just-in-time correlation now lives in Federation.** Measured against main, BCP 14 sentences go from 293 to 296 in Federation and from 45 to 43 in L; M is unchanged at 68 (`normative_diff`). Each requirement removed from L is preserved:

| Removed from L §4.1 | Now |
|---|---|
| "A Receiver MAY be configured to establish the local correlation from a validated ID-JAG" | F §6.3.1: "resource policy MAY permit the RAS to create one from a validated grant", for both ID-JAG and WAG; off by default, enabled per issuer and Target Tenant |
| "the RAS MAY create the local agent principal and its correlation keyed by the pair" | F §6.3.1: "MUST key the created record by that exact pair" |
| "MUST NOT attach the pair to an existing principal by name or other descriptive match" | F §6.3.1, same rule |
| "MUST apply Local Suspension, retained revocation state, and local policy before issuance" | F §6.3.1 "MUST apply local restrictions, retained revocation state ..., and local policy"; L names Local Suspension as one of those restrictions |
| "MUST subject the created principal to the same provisioning, reconciliation, and disablement rules" | Kept in L, together with a new MUST to expose the record with its `externalId` for reconciliation |

The Federation item in the "The RAS MUST" list that denies authorization depending on a missing agent record now points to F §6.3.1. Before, that MUST depended on behavior defined in L, which is only an informative reference of F. All three drafts build with no unresolved or uncited references and no over-long artwork lines.

## Applied

| Commit | Review item | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 043ca57, reverted by 584e92f | 10 | Just-in-time correlation was removed and then restored as a resource-policy option. Some resource domains cannot accept SCIM, and orchestration can deliver the first grant before provisioning completes. The removal rested on an overstated conflict. WAG §7 says the AS "MUST accept a previously-unseen Agent Identifier", with no opt-out. L §4.1 is a MAY, off by default, enabled per issuer and Target Tenant, never matched by descriptive attributes, and subject to Local Suspension. |
| 99ef254 | 10, and the re-review | F now says what the resource domain decides. §4.2 says a correlation is created from a grant only where resource policy permits. The RAS MUST list covers records created in advance or just in time. §10 and the WAG Linking gap contrast this with WAG's *required* acceptance. |
| 8e60f74 | re-review (P3) | The operational guidance names both just-in-time cases, user accounts and agent correlations, and points the agent case to L. |
| 2650ab7 | 10 | L §4.1 says an inactive initial state denies the triggering grant. A just-in-time record is visible with its `externalId`, so a later SCIM create gets `uniqueness`; the connector finds the record by query and updates it, and provisioning that lags the first grant converges on one principal. |
| 5fe0282 | 5, 6, 8 | L §1 names the revocation boundaries and Local Suspension. L §1.1 excludes runtime containment (executions, tool calls, network access, offline tokens before expiry). |
| 5533471 | 5 | L §8 becomes "Revocation Boundaries" and adds rows for Agent Principal disablement and Local Suspension, so the table covers every boundary. |
| 22fc37b | 1 | M §1: managing bindings and associations is authorization management, not descriptive provisioning. |
| 4f9e6eb | 11 | Each draft's introduction states the family relationship: management establishes the relationships at the IdP, federation exercises them, and lifecycle carries the principal's administrative state into the resource domain and revokes what depends on it. |
| 6a5e8fe | 11, closing | The README has a family diagram, the family sentence, and the "not one identity and one kill switch" framing. |
| b7b232c, c1fb2c3 | re-review (P2) | Conformance boundary. F §6.3.1 defines just-in-time correlation for both grants, with the policy gate, exact keying, and local restrictions and revocation state. A RAS without SCIM follows it and claims only F. L §4.1 keeps only what a conforming Receiver adds (SCIM exposure and reconciliation) and says a Receiver without the interface does not conform to L. This also closes the gap where F's WAG path pointed at an ID-JAG-only rule. |
| 70c4dce, 6c94eed, 999d7b4 | README | The README is now the landing page for all four drafts, with sections under each draft's title. It describes policy-gated just-in-time correlation. |

## Not applied as proposed

- **Item 10, moving JIT to an appendix or removing it.** The author's decision is that just-in-time correlation belongs in the base profile as a resource-side policy choice (see 584e92f).

- **"Lifecycle changes their continuing eligibility."** L does not manage binding or association state; that stays at the IdP under M, and L §1.1 excludes translating binding withdrawal into grants. The family sentence says what L does instead.
- **The same architecture section in every draft.** Three copies of one figure would drift. The figure is in the README, and each draft has the sentence.
- **Retitling M as "SCIM Profile for Governed Agent Management".** The general SCIM Agent resource belongs to SCIM-AGENT (I-D.wzdk-scim-agent-resource). M adds only the federation relationships: its extension is the "Agent Federation Extension" and its scope is delegated ID-JAG issuance. The title stays "SCIM Profile for Governed Agent Federation Management".

## Unchanged or deferred

- **Lifecycle title (item 9).** Kept, as the reviewer also advised. L §1.1 already disclaims a lifecycle state machine.
- **Items that endorse the current design (2, 3, 4, 7, 8).** No change; the missed-transition limits are preserved as written.
- **Blueprint four-question mapping (item 12).** This belongs in the README or WG slides, and no citation goes in without a stable URL.

pulls.title: Lead with the governed-identity boundary; ID-JAG and WAG as peers; RFC 7523bis audience
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Framing round in response to the "deployment profile first" review, plus a correctness fix the review did not raise. The consolidation round (the §5 and §8 trims, index tables, Governance Tenant) and the table-of-contents reorder follow in a separate PR.

## Framing (no requirement changes)

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| c33755e | The Abstract leads with the boundary between execution identity and governed identity, as an OAuth deployment profile. The identifiers can be the same or different. ID-JAG and WAG are presented as peer realizations. |
| 49f7502 | §1 states the defining proposition: the profile standardizes that boundary without requiring the two identities to differ, and a service provider can authorize a stable agent without understanding its runtime. A small figure shows an agent moving from workload-7 to workload-19 while the service provider still sees agent-42. |
| d1161f4 | Table 1 now lists each decision with its owner: which agent, may this client use it, and may it act (all decided by the IdP), and what it may do here (decided by the resource domain). |
| 9cd85eb | New §3.1, Service Provider Contract: what a resource domain receives from a grant, and that it never validates execution credentials. |
| 74dd974 | §6 says resolution can preserve the execution identifier; it establishes which identity is authoritative for governance. Before this, that was stated only in §3.3 and §8.4.4. |
| c109d89, b00f66f, 89d86e2 | Carried from the unpushed README branch: the §3.1 identity-continuity sentence and the README's architecture section. |

## WAG and ID-JAG as peers (author decision)

This reverses 062d97e ("Mark the self-acting WAG realization as a proposal throughout").

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| 9dfba06 | Peer wording in §1, §4.1, the §10 heading and introduction, the profile URIs, IANA, and the WAG coordination appendix. Only the WAG-owned token type and JWT type remain provisional values. |
| aab13a8 | **Requirement change.** Each realization has its own mandatory path. Delegated: ID Token subject, dedicated client, ID-JAG. Self-acting: dedicated client, WAG. Conformance claims name the realization, and the roles implement §8 or §10 for each realization they support. Before this, every role had to implement the delegated realization. |
| 2465d98 | §10.3 drops "interim". Presenting the authentication JWT as the subject token is the defined rule, and the Actor Profile's authentication-context reuse (§6.3.1) is the precedent. The X.509-SVID limit is stated as a limit of this profile. Asking WAG to allow omitting the subject token remains an optional simplification. |
| 4c102cf | README peer wording. |

## Correctness fix

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| 040aaeb | **Requirement change.** §5.1.2 required the token endpoint URL as the client assertion audience. draft-ietf-oauth-rfc7523bis-11 (in the RFC Editor queue) replaces RFC 7523 Section 3 item 3 for client authentication: "the aud (audience) claim value MUST use the issuer identifier ... as its sole value", "the token endpoint URL of the authorization server MUST NOT be used as an audience value", and "The authorization server MUST reject any JWT that does not contain its issuer identifier as its sole audience value." §5.1.2 now requires following that section. The input table and the walkthrough example are updated, and RFC7523bis is added as a normative reference. With one fixed audience, the local retry-with-another-audience rules no longer apply. |

## Requirement accounting

BCP 14 sentences go from 296 to 291; keywords go from 325 to 319 (`normative_diff`, against this branch's base).

- Reworded for per-realization conformance: the Roles, Issuance, conformance-claim, and API rules.
- Replaced by the pointer to 7523bis (a dependency restatement): the seven audience rules, 4 MUST, 2 MUST NOT, 1 MAY.
- Reworded without "interim": the self-acting subject-token MUST.

The build is clean and the idnits output is unchanged. The page count stays at 114, because the framing adds text; the size reduction comes in the consolidation PR.

comments.author: mcguinness
comments.body:
Fixed both review findings on this branch:

- c322e89: the RAS advertises the base ID-JAG profile only for delegated access. The IdP advertises ID-JAG issuance only for delegated access, and the WAG token type for self-acting access, so a WAG-only server no longer advertises capabilities it doesn't support.
- fec1955: the walkthrough's redemption assertion now uses `aud=https://ras.example/` (RFC 7523bis §4). DPoP `htu` keeps the token endpoint.

#4 already carried the same fixes; this branch is merged into it (f1501b4) with #4's text unchanged.

pulls.title: Consolidate: interface-contract inputs, delegated base rules, peer realizations, conformance last
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Consolidation round from the "deployment profile first" review. It is stacked on #3; merge #3 first.

## Result

| | Base (4c102cf) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Pages | 114 | 104 |
| Body words | 21,136 | 18,158 (−14%) |
| Appendix words | 3,738 | 4,700, including the moved optional inputs |
| BCP 14 keywords, whole document | 319 | 309 |

## Method

A fixed record of all 319 BCP 14 occurrences was taken at the base, each with its previous sentence and paragraph lead. Three editors worked under frozen rules: no new requirements, conditions travel with their keyword, and every delegation to a base specification quotes the target sentence that carries the same obligation. They covered resolution inputs, ID-JAG issuance, and ID-JAG redemption plus API processing, and each produced a change ledger. A read-only verifier then aligned every recorded obligation with the result:

| Class | Count |
|---|---|
| Same | 261 |
| Restructured, same obligation | 52 |
| Delegated, dependency sentence verified | 2 (#39 RFC 7523 §3; #185 ID-JAG §4.3.3) |
| Changed | 1 (#91, below) |
| Missing | 0 |

Three delegations (#162, #165, #167, DPoP proof validation and binding) were restored as local requirements. ID-JAG §9.8.1 covers only the ID-JAG, and grant protection also governs WAG. A consistency reader then checked cross-references, terminology, and peer treatment after the moves. Its findings are fixed in the commits listed below. The fix commits got a targeted check (every keyword sentence diffed against the reviewed tree), not a second full verification.

## Structure

- §3 Federation Model now holds Grant Paths, Adoption Profiles (split out of the old Scope and Conformance unit), Federation Configuration, and the example.
- §4 Agent Principal Resolution opens with Agent Resolution Inputs. The inputs open with an interface contract; the dedicated-client and platform JWT inputs stay in the body.
- Appendix A, Optional Agent Resolution Inputs, is **normative** and holds JWT-SVID, Client Attestation, WIT-SVID and X.509-SVID, and resolution-key lifecycle.
- §6 Delegated Access with ID-JAG and §7 Self-Acting Access with WAG sit side by side as peers.
- §8 Conformance and Metadata closes the body.
- The Core Invariants and Requirements by Implementer index tables are removed.

## Requirement changes

Removed (13, each in the ledgers):
- **Delegated:** #39 and #185, with dependency quotes verified.
- **Duplicates, each with one home kept:** for example #87 (duplicate of `{#inputs}` and `{#identity-binding}`), #239, and the WAG acting-relationship MUST (kept in API processing).
- **Error-table rows:** codes already defined by RFC 7523, RFC 9449, or another unit of this draft.
- **Algorithm table:** the JWT access token row, which pointed to RFC 9068 §2.1 ("MUST include RS256").

Changed or added, all deliberate:
- **#91:** the proof-binding example now names the WIT-SVID input instead of "the SVID inputs". The base itself says an X.509-SVID "certificate does not endorse the DPoP key".
- **Scope clarifications that follow from peer status:** the presented-evidence definition says "In delegated issuance" (WAG presents that evidence as the subject token and forbids `actor_token`); the API Identity bullet says "For delegated tokens"; the Actor Profile metadata-consistency rule says "For delegated access".
- **New:** IdP metadata advertises the WAG token type for self-acting access, as a use proposed for coordination ({{wag-gaps}}). Before this, self-acting clients had no discovery.
- **Conformance roles:** now name {{security}} and the normative appendix, and the requirements apply to "this document" rather than "below".

## Consistency fixes

- Pointers into shortened or moved units now point to where the rule lives: `{{configuration}}`, `{{distributed-key-use}}`, `{{optional-input-profiles}}`, `{{imported-jwt-input}}`, `{{baseline-costs}}`, and the new `{{redemption-example}}`.
- The authorization-details error row is restored, citing RFC 9396 §8. Two editors had each removed half of it, each relying on the other.
- Appendix C.3 now uses the issuer audience `https://ras.example/`, per RFC 7523bis.
- The security text covers self-acting access in its client-key compromise and bearer-evidence cases.
- The adoption-profile table distinguishes a delegated actor from a self-acting subject.
- The WAG section states its X.509-SVID exception.
- The resolution mode is named "presented-evidence" for both grants, replacing "actor-evidence" and "presented workload".
- `Section 9 of OPENID` is kept in prose form, because xml2rfc cannot link a section of a hand-written reference.

## Not changed

- Grant-derived revocation (Security §9.6) still names ID-JAGs. The lifecycle companion defines it for ID-JAG only, so extending it to WAG belongs in that companion.
- idnits `SECTION_TITLE_HAS_UNEXPECTED_INDENTATION` rose from 8 to 11. These come from xml2rfc's table-of-contents lines for numbered appendices, not from the draft text.

pulls.title: Framing touch-ups: service-provider-first abstract, same identifier up front, interoperable contract
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Small framing edits from the latest review, which confirmed that the "different `sub`" reading no longer fits and asked to make the interoperability boundary more prominent. No requirement changes (BCP 14 keywords stay at 309).

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| 39098d3 | The Abstract opens with the service provider's need: a stable identity for an enterprise-governed agent without understanding its runtime, workload credential, or OAuth client. |
| 01a14fb | Where §1 first describes Identity Binding, and in the Identity Binding definition, the draft says the Agent Principal can have the same identifier as the execution identity. Before this, the statement appeared later in §1 and in §4. |
| fea3f59 | §3.1 opens with the answer to "what are we standardizing": the mapping is local to the IdP, and the security contract across the IdP-to-resource boundary is interoperable. |
| 0fa2268 | §6 opens by pointing to §6.1 as the list of every change to ID-JAG, with the sections after it giving the processing rule behind each row. |

Two further steps from the same review follow as stacked PRs: a requirements audit (whether another party relies on each requirement), and an appendix restructure.

pulls.title: Requirements audit: keep what another party relies on, demote internal duties
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Requirements audit from the latest review, which said parts of the draft read as normative requirements on internal authorization-server behavior. Stacked on #5.

## The test

A requirement stays normative if another party relies on it. That keeps every IdP issuance condition, because those define what an issued grant asserts, which the RAS relies on: resolution through an enabled Identity Binding, the Client Association check, and delegation or agent authorization. It also keeps wire behavior, validation at receipt, error codes, and security rules whose violation yields authority that a counterparty honors. Configuration, storage, caching internals, audit logging, documentation, and administration duties become deployment guidance or stated trust assumptions, keeping their substance and conditions.

## Result

BCP 14 keywords go from 309 to 282. The audit demoted 29 occurrences (MUST −13, MUST NOT −3, SHOULD −6, MAY −7), and verification restored or added two. Five requirements were reworded to state the relied-upon outcome with the same keyword.

Main demotions, each with the normative outcome that still carries it:
- Execution-independence rules (scaling, restarts, and rotation do not increase authority) remain carried by the §5 authorization rules.
- Provisioning SHOULDs: RAS behavior once a change is applied remains normative.
- Target Tenant carrier agreement is now a stated trust assumption.
- Audit-record and "document your disablement delay" duties.
- Provenance input choice: the RAS cannot see which input was used (§3.1).
- Configuration latitude MAYs now say "can": multiple bindings per agent, deployment topology, and how the actor gate is implemented.
- WAG identity retention is RAS practice, because no token or introspection member carries it.

## Verification

An independent verifier checked every changed entry for kept substance and conditions, and confirmed that each claimed backstop exists and carries the obligation. 23 were confirmed. Fixed after verification:
- **#285 restored:** the IdP MUST apply a change within a configured freshness limit on cached policy data. Without it, a disabled agent could keep receiving grants that the RAS honors.
- **#11 split:** delegations do not carry forward to a new identifier, and **new: RAS principal links held for the previous identifier MUST NOT be re-keyed** to the new one. The claimed backstop did not cover re-keying.
- **#281:** replay state stays in effect "where a mechanism retains replay state", so the rule no longer requires replay detection on grants that may be redeemed repeatedly.
- **#39:** the platform JWT's issuer, credential class, and authenticated client are configured together.
- **The policy-service rule:** for a self-acting token, the local principal stands for the Agent Principal.
- **Applied-changes invalidation:** stated as the MUST, with retention from issuance.

The fix commits got a targeted check against the verifier's findings, not a second full verification.

pulls.title: Move input profiles to appendices and condense coordination notes
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Appendix restructure from the latest review. Stacked on the audit PR.

- **Mandatory inputs to a normative appendix:** dedicated-client identity and the existing platform JWT now sit in Appendix A, "Mandatory Agent Resolution Inputs", before the optional inputs (Appendix B). §4.1 keeps the interface contract, the input table, and the bearer-evidence limits, so the body reads as model, contract, and grants. The conformance Roles bullet names the new appendix. No requirement text changed.
- **Dependencies appendix condensed:** every cited anchor is kept, with shorter coordination notes. The full notes, including the detailed WAG, ID-JAG, and Actor Profile coordination asks, move to `COORDINATION.md` in the repository until adoption.

Honest measurement: the page count stays at 104. Moving text does not shorten the document, and the dependencies appendix is mostly tables. The body is 17,271 words, 5% below `main`. Further page reduction would mean dropping the walkthrough's rejection-examples table (about 2 pages, which mirrors the error tables) or moving the optional inputs to a companion draft (about 4 pages). Both are left for the author.

pulls.title: Presentation cut: 15% shorter with every obligation verified
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
A presentation-only cut, following the 25% cut strategy with interoperability preservation as the acceptance gate. It is stacked on #7 (#5, #6, #7).

## Result

| | Base (7f69e83) | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Source words, main text and appendices | 22,823 | 19,301 (−15.4%) |
| Rendered pages | 104 | 90 |
| BCP 14 keywords | 282 | 288, of which 2 come from the open-issue resolutions |

The cut stops short of the 20% first target. Seven region editors and a cross-region deduplication pass each independently reached the same floor: the remaining text states rules found nowhere else, or it is security analysis, examples, or the configuration table. The strategy says to go past that only while an implementer can still find the required request, validation, output, and failure behavior as easily. Cutting further would mean removing unique content, so it is left for the author to decide.

| Area | Before | After | Budget |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Introduction and terminology | 1,935 | 1,550 | 1,300 |
| Federation model | 3,085 | 2,494 | 1,900 |
| Resolution and authorization | 2,843 | 2,422 | 2,250 |
| ID-JAG and WAG processing | 6,542 | 6,150 | 5,200 |
| Conformance and metadata | 1,226 | 985 | 950 |
| Security, privacy, IANA | 1,677 | 1,587 | 1,400 |
| Input appendices | 2,007 | 1,827 | 1,700 |
| Dependencies | 899 | 603 | 450 |
| Walkthrough and variants | 2,609 | 1,960 | 1,950 |

These are the four-pass figures; the later deduplication and fix commits moved the total to 19,301.

## Method

1. **Contract first.** An obligation ledger of 458 obligations (party, stage, flow or profile, condition, outcome, exception, failure response, home) was built on the base. It includes 90 rules without a BCP 14 keyword and 71 held in table cells.
2. **Four passes, as seven region editors under frozen rules.** Protocol behavior was frozen: each obligation stays intact, is consolidated into an equivalent rule, or is inherited from a dependency whose sentence is quoted. Each pass is one commit:
   - Pass 1, introduction and model (f5c3e51);
   - Pass 2, resolution and grant processing (c3ae820);
   - Pass 3, inputs, conformance, and security (1d622b0);
   - Pass 4, examples and coordination (7859f8b).
3. **Cross-region deduplication.** The ledger found 162 obligations stated in two places. The pass removed duplicates across region boundaries in 14 commits. Two proposals were rejected: removing the "Relationship to Base Specifications" narrowing table, and removing the delegated-versus-self-acting comparison table. Both stay.
4. **Verification.** Three obligation verifiers checked all 458 ledger rows, and two implementer traces worked through the representative cases. Findings were fixed in the commits after the passes.

## Verification results

- **Obligations:** 0 missing. One changed: O-399, where a `private_key_jwt`-only condition was broadened to every RFC 7523 method. It is fixed in df2093f.
- **WAG inheritance:** the blanket clause ("where this section is silent, the delegated section applies") is replaced by explicit references in each WAG unit. The grant verifier mapped every delegated rule a WAG IdP, RAS, or API relied on and found no gaps.
- **Implementer traces:** every case was the same or easier, except configuring the shared-client platform JWT. That became harder when its configuration table was split, and df2093f puts it back in one place. The self-acting path is easier than before: the RAS now rejects a WAG carrying `act` explicitly, where the old inheritance pointed it at a rule that requires `act`.
- **Fix commits:** they got a targeted check (every keyword sentence diffed against the verified snapshot), not a second full verification.

## Keyword changes (282 → 286)

- **+8 MUST:** the input appendices split shared leads ("Configuration MUST also specify:", "The IdP MUST also:") into one MUST per item. The verifier confirmed none gained or lost a condition.
- **−2 MUST:** the platform JWT configuration items are merged back under one lead.
- **−3:** three issuance sentences are consolidated into their homes (wag-claims `act`, grant-issuance `cnf.jkt` and lifetime).
- **+1 MUST NOT:** the WAG unambiguous-context rule is stated explicitly instead of through inheritance.

The net +4 is not the whole story. The following requirements are also new normative text, and some carry no keyword of their own, for example a step under a "The RAS MUST:" lead.

## Requirements previously stated only in examples or through inheritance, now normative

The strategy requires that "any unique condition found only in an example must first acquire an authoritative definition". These are those definitions, plus the rules that the blanket WAG inheritance used to carry implicitly. Several add a failure code to a normative table for the first time:

- The RAS rejects a WAG that contains `act` with `invalid_grant`, and wag-errors has a row for it. The old inheritance pointed the RAS at a rule that *requires* `act`.
- A token tenant different from the operation's tenant gets HTTP 401 `invalid_token` (previously only in an example).
- An X.509-SVID supplied only as request data fails client authentication (previously only in an example).
- A reused dedicated-client assertion fails client authentication, which is how RFC 7523 §3.2's `invalid_client` applies (previously only in an example).
- Where RAS refresh is permitted, a new ID-JAG after the absolute expiration starts a new period and leaves the previous expiration unchanged (previously only in an example).
- A WAG redemption never yields a refresh token (stated in ras-refresh; the WAG section already prohibited it).
- Grant protection states that it applies to both grants.

## Presentation changes

- A reading guide for all roles, the client, the IdP, the RAS, and the API.
- Federation Configuration is now a table of relationship, configuring authority, and required context.
- One figure shows both grant paths, and one claim-transformation example remains.
- Processing units use short labels (Applicability, Inputs, Validation, Output, Failures).
- Every input profile uses the same labeled layout.
- The input table has a resolution-mode column.
- "ID-JAG Redemption" is renamed "Redemption", since its subsections serve both grants.
- The walkthrough keeps six representative rejection cases.
- The dependencies appendix is condensed; the full notes are in COORDINATION.md.

## Open issues, resolved in this PR

| Issue | Resolution | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| The walkthrough said WIT-SVID and X.509-SVID bindings "carry their own permission" | Every variant needs a Client Association. In the WIT-SVID and X.509-SVID variants the authenticated client is the workload itself, so the association can be administered together with the binding, as the SCIM profile does for dedicated clients. This restores the original intent in terms the body supports. | c04186a |
| Is a WAG subject token containing `act` rejected? | Yes. The existing inbound actor chain rule ("reject an agent-resolution JWT … containing `act`") applies. The WAG text now says only actor construction and the governed `act` result are excluded. No new requirement. | 48f3caf |
| DPoP or bearer when a resource permits both | **New MUST.** Where the effective client and resource configuration leaves a choice only between DPoP and bearer, the RAS binds the access token to a valid DPoP proof presented at redemption, and issues bearer only when no proof is presented. Configured mutual TLS takes precedence over any DPoP proof, including the grant proof. A proof never selects a protection that configuration does not permit. RFC 9449 §5 lets a server issue bearer even with a proof, so the profile makes the safer choice explicit. | 715ffd1, 79e5256 |
| Platform JWT audiences are configured but other values are not rejected | **New MUST.** The IdP rejects a platform JWT whose `aud` is absent or contains none of the configured audiences. When `aud` is present, this is RFC 7519 §4.1.3's rejection; the profile adds the absent case. | 4bcf2ab |
| A grant-lifetime row contradicting WAG was deleted rather than reconciled | The dedicated-client row is restored as "None: it authenticates one request and does not cap the grant", without the subject-credential wording that did not fit WAG. | 71722ed |

These two new MUSTs bring the keyword count to 288. A later commit (0a55156) also replaces the Federation Configuration table with labeled entries grouped by responsible party, for readability.

The remaining open question for the author is whether to reach 20% by cutting unique content; see the levers above.

pulls.title: Simplify the densest paragraphs, bullets, and tables
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Readability pass on the densest paragraphs, bullets, and tables. It is presentation-only: protocol behavior is frozen.

## Result

| | Before (926a44b) | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Prose sentences over 30 words | 78 | 11 |
| Prose sentences over 40 words | 16 | 0 |
| Longest prose sentence (words) | 69 | 38 |
| Table cells over 20 words | 8 | 0 |
| Densest item (density score) | 211 | 149 |
| Words (main body, fenced blocks excluded) | 19,024 | 19,172 (+0.8%) |
| Rendered pages | 90 | 93 |

Sentences are counted per paragraph and per bullet, splitting after `.`, `;`, or `:`. Nested bullets count separately.

Pages rose because bullet lists take more vertical space than dense paragraphs.

## Method

A density ranking scored every paragraph, bullet, and table row by length, longest sentence, citations, and keywords. Six editors worked the ranking in their regions, densest first, under frozen rules:
- one requirement per sentence;
- dense multi-condition paragraphs become short bullets or numbered steps under a lead;
- table cells become phrases, with explanation moved to a sentence after the table;
- no region grows more than 3%;
- every condition travels with its rule.

Each region is one commit:

| Commit | Region | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 5a24dba | Introduction, terminology, model | Introduction sentences split; Roles companions and out-of-scope items as lists; transfer rule as a lead with bullets; adoption-table cells shortened |
| 043d00b | Resolution and authorization | Agent Authorization split into short sentences; actor-preservation rules as bullets; JIT correlation plainer; inputs table back to three columns with the mode in a sentence |
| a9ecaa6 | Delegated grant | Access-token selection as a lead with labeled bullets; "Grant protection by profile" table as two bullets; policy-service and applicability rules as bullets; error-table rows split |
| a650634 | Self-acting grant | The densest paragraph in the draft (WAG authentication-context resolution, 139 words) became five bullets; the comparison table's longest cell went from 16 words to 9; a missing blank line that folded the "Differences from Delegated Access" heading is fixed |
| 48171b3 | Conformance and security | The nine-citation conformance sentence became a lead with bullets; disablement limits became four bullets; tradeoff cells shortened |
| 330dbe2 | Appendices | The WAG coordination sentence (69 words, seven citations) became five bullets; retry and validation bullets split; input-variant notes as labeled bullets; rejection cells shortened |

## Verification

Two read-only verifiers checked every changed BCP 14 sentence, table row, and bullet list against the recorded baseline: party, condition, outcome, exception, and failure response.
- **Grants and appendices:** 179 entries, 0 changed. Every error-table trigger keeps its code. The delicate rules are intact:
  - DPoP-versus-bearer selection with mutual TLS precedence;
  - the refresh-token rule order;
  - the WAG byte-identical subject token, X.509-SVID exclusion, and inbound-actor rejection;
  - replay and retry.

  Two precision nits from sentence splits are fixed in 8f362d1: the JWT-SVID signature timing, and the WIT-SVID thumbprint objects.
- **Body:** 101 sentences, one changed in form only. The Agent Authorization rejection rule had moved into a paragraph without its "For self-acting access" condition. It is rejoined in 6d1c4aa.

## Keywords (288 → 293)

All five additions come from declared splits of compound requirements, each keeping its condition:
- Agent Authorization timing (+1 MUST);
- conformance issuance (+1 MUST);
- JWT-SVID validation (+1 MUST);
- WIT-SVID validation (+2 MUST).

No keyword was removed, weakened, or swapped. Apparent MUST/MUST NOT shifts in Agent Authorization and Discovery are counting artifacts: in the base, a "MUST" and "NOT" pair sat across a line break.

## Left dense on purpose

The editors' ledgers record these passages as kept, because splitting them would change what a reader infers:
- **Identity Binding tuple** (client, binding, credential class, acting relationship). Split up, it reads as separate permissions that could be satisfied one at a time.
- **Issuance decision over eight inputs** (Authorization Relationship). As a list, it reads as eight independent authorizations.
- **DPoP-or-bearer selection sentence** (38 words). It is kept verbatim to protect its condition.
- **Subject Token Validation lead.** Splitting it would repeat the {{Section 4.3.3 of ID-JAG}} qualifier.
- **Effects of administrative changes table, rows 1 and 6 and the new-authorization column.** They carry scope and timing conditions. The other cells were trimmed.
- **"Additions and narrowings" table and the reading-guide table.** They are already phrase lists of pointers; trimming would drop items.

The Grant Validation "Authority" step still has the top density score (149). The script scores the whole nested list as one unit; its longest sentence fell from 45 to 30 words. Some lines over 72 columns predate this PR and were left as they were.

pulls.title: Organize the core draft by protocol stage with ID-JAG and WAG as peers
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Reorganizes the core draft by protocol stage, with the processing role in each chapter heading. Delegated access (ID-JAG) and self-acting access (WAG) become sibling cases at every stage. The goal is to make the reading guide (Table 1) unnecessary and to stop WAG reading as a patch on ID-JAG.

## New outline

| Chapter | Contents |
|---|---|
| 3 Federation Model | Model, canonical identity, grant paths with the delegated/self-acting comparison, authorization relationships (Agent and Delegation Authorization, lifetime, actor gate) |
| 4 Profiles, Configuration, and Conformance | ID-JAG and WAG overviews, adoption profiles, grant protection, conformance, algorithms, time/replay/key validation, token endpoint error conventions, configuration, metadata and discovery |
| 5 Grant Issuance at the IdP | Prerequisites, common token exchange request, agent resolution, issuance authorization, common grant claims/lifetime/response, **Delegated Issuance: ID-JAG**, **Self-Acting Issuance: WAG**, issuance errors |
| 6 Grant Redemption at the RAS | Redemption request, common grant validation, agent correlation (JIT), **Delegated Redemption: ID-JAG**, **Self-Acting Redemption: WAG**, access token issuance, protection, key use, introspection, redemption errors |
| 7 Access at the Resource Server | Applicability, token validation, **Delegated Access**, **Self-Acting Access**, policy services, errors |
| 8 Continuing Access and Authorization Changes | Renewal, client token reuse, RAS refresh, applied disablement |

The appendices are regrouped: A. input profiles (required, optional); B. worked exchanges and input variants; C. dependencies.

## How it was done

1. **Move only (d04b252).** Whole sections move under new headings. The paragraph set is identical before and after (442 paragraphs), and every keyword and anchor is kept.
2. **Role splits (890114f).** Mixed IdP/RAS sections split at paragraph level, each keeping its "The IdP MUST:" or "the RAS MUST:" lead. Pointers are retargeted where a target split. Two sentences the move made false are reworded.
3. **Peer wording (8e4117c to 582a132).** One commit per change:
   - common request, claims and lifetime, redemption checks, and per-stage errors;
   - access-token identity, introspection, and token reuse state both grants;
   - parallel resource-server sections for delegated and self-acting access;
   - the WAG "Shared rules" list, the "as in the delegated section" wording, and "Of the limits in … apply" are removed.
4. **Reading guide (8b2daf9, 1de4d93).** Table 1 becomes a one-paragraph roadmap that names each stage chapter. For the client it says that client requirements accompany the requests and responses at each stage; the headings carry the rest.
5. **Verification fixes (7fc272c, bb5f968, 6d8cde4, 8d7c980, 4419ea9)**, from three independent checks.
6. **Review of #10 (1de4d93, 6dd5ac3).** The interim five-item client list is replaced by one sentence. RAS refresh processing moves, unchanged, to chapter 8, with a pointer from the initial access-token response.

## Verification

- **Requirements check:** every keyword sentence was compared with `main`. It found two regressions, both fixed:
  - the WAG request's own parameters had lost the REQUIRED they inherited;
  - moving the checks into one common block had reordered them, which would change the error a request failing two checks gets.
- **Cold route trace:** eight paths (IdP, RAS, API, and client, for each grant). Fixes from it:
  - the IdP lifetime-condition rule was stranded in §3;
  - the WAG issuance steps did not cite issuance authorization;
  - just-in-time correlation said the actor gate applies to self-acting tokens;
  - the correlation pair was named only for ID-JAG;
  - two error rows overlapped;
- **Check of the fix commits:** two follow-ups (a table-row scope and an appendix pointer), both fixed.
- **Build:** clean, with no unresolved or uncited references. The idnits categories are unchanged from `main`.

## Requirement wording to review

Every edit to requirement text is listed here so any one can be dropped:

| Change | Effect |
|---|---|
| Keywords 293 → 296 | +1 REQUIRED for the common request table; +1 REQUIRED on the WAG request, restoring what WAG inherited; +1 MUST for the delegated API lead |
| "shorter **ID-JAG** lifetime" → "shorter **grant** lifetime" in the lifetime-condition MUST NOT | Deliberate extension to WAG; the rule's first sentence already covered self-acting issuance |
| Delegated Client Association error row scoped "for delegated issuance" | Removes overlap with the self-acting `unauthorized_client` row |
| Just-in-time correlation: actor gate "for delegated access" | Removes the contradiction with "no actor gate" for self-acting tokens |
| Credential-class selection "for presented evidence" (was "actor evidence") | WAG already applied the rule to its subject token |
| Two lifetime-condition error rows | The codes the rule already stated |
| Issuance error tables read as the IdP's | The old single table named no server |
| Common redemption checks have no MUST of their own | Each grant's numbered steps require them, in the original order |
| WAG request based on RFC 8693 rather than ID-JAG Section 4.3 | Left as is |

Size: 93 → 95 pages, 19,602 → 19,826 words (+1.1%). This round reorganizes rather than shortens.

## Gaps found by the trace, not caused by this PR (follow-up)

- **RAS:** no error code for its own denials:
  - actor-gate denial at redemption;
  - WAG local-policy denial;
  - missing agent record;
  - applied disablement;
  - a just-in-time record created ineligible;
  - a client/`client_id` mismatch.
- **API:**
  - no code for ambiguous applicability;
  - no rule rejecting a self-acting token that carries `act`;
  - no row for denial under the agent's own permissions.
- **IdP:** no code for an unsupported `subject_token_type`.
- **WAG:**
  - no `typ` check at redemption;
  - the dedicated-client appendix doesn't mention repeating the assertion as `subject_token`, and its retry and replay rules cover only the IdP;
  - re-redemption of a valid WAG is not addressed.
- **Security:**
  - the admin-effects table has no row for withdrawing Agent Authorization;
  - the propagation text covers only ID-JAGs.
- **WAG rules still defined through ID-JAG sections** (9.8.1.x, 3.1, 4.3.4, 4.4.2). Already tracked in COORDINATION.md.

pulls.title: Fix WAG type confusion, WAG-01 citations, and RAS replay before trimming
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Fixes found while analyzing the draft for trimming. They go first because they correct the contract that the trim will be checked against. Each fix is its own commit.

## Fixes

| Commit | Fix | Requirement change |
|---|---|---|
| 554a6e4 | **The RAS now checks the WAG's explicit type** (`typ` `wag+jwt`, RFC 8725 §3.11) at redemption. Both grants are JWTs redeemed with `jwt-bearer`. Previously an ID-JAG with no `act` from the same IdP could be processed as a WAG and, with just-in-time correlation enabled, create an agent record from a user's `sub`. WAG-01 defines no explicit type and flags this risk (§§8–9). Credential and Token Confusion now notes how the RAS tells the grants apart. | Adds one check under the existing "The RAS MUST:" lead |
| 5d6e49e | **WAG-01 alignment.** "Section 7 of WAG" (acceptance of unseen agents) now cites §3, where WAG-01 describes it; it is no longer called "required". "Section 5 anticipates IdP issuance" becomes "the IdP is WAG's Platform (§2)". The type open item cites §8. The IANA note no longer says WAG proposes the registrations (WAG-01 has no IANA actions). The appendix and COORDINATION.md now say they were assessed against WAG-01. | None |
| 1323c30 | **Re-redemption.** The renewal table said any valid ID-JAG can be redeemed again. Actor Profile §4.2 rejects a reused `jti` for a grant carrying `act` when redemption requires neither DPoP nor mutual TLS, so an unbound governed ID-JAG redeems once. The table now says so. | None (non-normative table) |
| 1fc7d4b | **Replay at the RAS.** The dedicated-client input's Audience rule already binds both servers, but its Replay rule named only the IdP. RFC 7523 leaves `jti` checking optional, so a replayed client assertion plus a stolen unbound grant could be redeemed. Replay and Retry now apply at either server. | The RAS gains the IdP's single-use `jti` MUST (an existing MUST, not a new keyword) |
| 3509f43 | Small fixes: the example B2 ARN now matches the AWS example it cites; the self-acting walkthrough says the redemption uses a fresh client assertion and DPoP proof; the `invalid_grant` note covers subject credentials, as the error table already did, and cites ID-JAG's error example. | None |

Build clean at 95 pages. No body keyword sentences changed (224 → 224); the one changed requirement is the Appendix A replay rule above.

## Decisions for the author (recorded in COORDINATION.md, not changed here)

1. **Re-redemption.** ID-JAG §4.4.3 lets clients re-submit an ID-JAG; Actor Profile §4.2 forbids re-submitting an unbound one carrying `act`. Keep Actor Profile's rule (the table now reflects it), or relax it in Actor Profile for grants whose client is authenticated.
2. **WAG-01 §5: "MUST NOT require a client registration per Agent."** The mandatory path resolves one Agent Principal per dedicated client at the IdP. Decide whether that conflicts at the RAS, where the same client redeems the WAG.
3. **WAG-01 §5: access tokens "SHOULD NOT outlive the assertion by a significant period."** This draft leaves access-token lifetime to RAS policy. Adopt the SHOULD, or state the difference.

## Next: trimming

The trim analysis (six region ledgers, verified dependency quotes) estimates about 4,000 words (about 95 → 75 pages) that can leave without losing interoperability or security:
- delegation to dependencies: about 450 words;
- deleting and merging restatements, navigation, and duplicated examples: about 2,700;
- moving configuration guidance and examples out of the requirements text: about 2,500 more.

That follows in separate PRs, after this one.

pulls.title: Trim restatements and move configuration guidance out of the requirements
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Stacked on #11. This trims text that fails the test: if this text disappeared, could two independent implementations still interoperate correctly and securely under the same attackers? Each removal is one of three things:
- a verified duplicate with a named kept copy;
- a delegation whose dependency text was quoted;
- a navigation or explanatory sentence with no requirement.

No requirement is demoted.

## Result

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pages | 95 | 92 |
| Whole document (words) | 19,934 | 19,424 (−510) |
| Body | 15,454 | 14,409 (−1,045) |
| Body without code blocks and tables | 13,044 | 12,213 (−831) |
| Requirements text (body minus the new non-normative section) | 15,454 | about 13,730 (−11%) |
| BCP 14 keywords | 296 | 293 (3 MUST, each kept elsewhere) |

## What changed

**New Implementation Considerations section (non-normative), before Security Considerations.** It holds these sections, moved verbatim with their anchors:
- **Federation Configuration.** Its two governance-core MUST NOTs stay normative, moved verbatim into "Authentication, Resolution, and Proof": discovery does not establish trust, and hints or unverified claims do not change a binding or association.
- **Distributed Platforms and Key Use.**

**Moved to appendices:**
- the Identity Mapping Example and the multi-binding example, to Appendix B;
- the input index table, to Appendix A's preamble.

**Removed requirement sentences, each kept elsewhere:**

| Removed | Kept copy |
|---|---|
| "The request MUST contain exactly one `resource` parameter" | The common request table's "Exactly one resource URI" row under its REQUIRED lead; the IdP's `invalid_target` rejection stays |
| The ID Token audience MUST | The list lead's delegation to ID-JAG §4.3.3, which requires it (ID-JAG path only) |
| "The API MUST enforce that `cnf` as it would the JWT claim" | API Token Validation: "enforce … all token confirmation claims", for JWT or introspected context |

**Delegations, none carrying a keyword:**
- unknown parameters: RFC 6749 §3.2, RFC 7519 §4;
- SPIFFE authentication-method metadata: SPIFFE-OAUTH §4;
- inactive introspection for revoked authorization: RFC 7662;
- `aud` rejection when present: RFC 7519 §4.1.3.

**Deletions:**
- navigation sentences that the stage headings made redundant;
- about 20 restatements, each with a named kept copy;
- a few explanatory sentences.

**Follow-ups from verification (673be24):**
- The IdP's "issue only under the applicable relationships" MUST now cites the model instead of the moved configuration section.
- The Client Association check cites Terms.
- "Agent Resolution Inputs" points to Appendix A.
- A lost antecedent is fixed.
- The multi-binding example is aligned with its neighbors.
- Chapter 4 is retitled "Profiles and Conformance".

## How it was checked

1. Six region analyses applied the interop and security test. A reconciler then verified each proposal:
   - quotes matched against the text;
   - every duplicate's kept copy located;
   - every dependency quote found in the cached texts;
   - moved blocks checked to carry no keywords.

   It kept 43 items and skipped 229, with a reason recorded for each.
2. An independent verifier confirmed:
   - all 43 items were applied as planned and nothing else changed;
   - the RECORD shows exactly three requirement sentences gone, each with its kept copy;
   - the moved sections carry no keywords;
   - the two MUST NOTs moved verbatim.
3. Build clean; no reference or anchor lost.

## Why this is smaller than the estimate of about 4,000 words

The analysts' raw proposals came to about 6,400 words. Most of that was sentence compression, which works against the readability pass (#9), or it removed requirements without an exact duplicate. Also skipped: text that PRs #8 and #10 deliberately kept or restored.

## Opt-ins for the author (not applied)

- **Rule-valid items that recent PRs kept or restored:** 39 items, about 900 words. Examples:
  - Governance Boundary restatements, which would also let the rest of that section move to Implementation Considerations (about 210);
  - the three-identities paragraph (69);
  - the Input Variants table (89);
  - redemption example details (about 125);
  - about 15 sibling-to-common navigation links added in #10.

  The full list is in the plan.
- **Demotions:** about 15 MUSTs that bind a party only to its own configuration or state. Examples: skew versus maximum age, the cached-policy freshness limit, "RAS MUST limit lifetimes under local policy", and the IdP metadata MUSTs.
- **Tables and examples:**
  - Adoption Tradeoffs (about 1.5 pages);
  - the rejection-examples table (about 1 page);
  - Appendix C coordination notes already in COORDINATION.md.
- **Moving optional inputs to a companion draft:** about 6 pages out of this document, about 9 pages into a new one.

pulls.title: Compose client instance identification and attester endorsement
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Client Instance Identification (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-instance-id-00`) and Client Attester Endorsement (`draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-attesters-00`) are now published. This PR composes them with the governed-agent drafts. An instance is treated as an execution of the agent's client, never as a governed principal. It is evidence beside the agent, for audit and containment.

Both drafts already fit this model:
- Our model keeps the Agent Principal independent of executions.
- The instance draft says instance identity "grants no authority" and forbids setting `sub` or `act` from instance evidence.
- The instance draft's Appendix A.3 shows the governed-actor case: `act.sub` = agent-42, with `client_instance` naming the presenting instance.

## Core draft

| Where | Change | Keywords |
|---|---|---|
| Identity Binding | A client instance identifier, or another identifier of one execution, MUST NOT select or change the Agent Principal or satisfy a Client Association | +1 MUST NOT |
| Client Attestation input | The IdP MAY derive the attester-to-client association from an endorsement it accepts under ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT §2.1. An endorsement MUST NOT create or change an Identity Binding or Client Association. Bindings name the attester, so a newly endorsed attester resolves no agent until a binding names it. An accepted endorsement is not "client metadata acting by itself" (§3.2) | +1 MAY, +1 MUST NOT |
| Client Attestation input (note) | Instance keys differ per receiver scope, and a bound grant carries the IdP-scoped key. A client that also authenticates to the RAS with a Client Attestation uses `attest_jwt_client_auth` there, with a separate DPoP proof, unless the IdP and RAS share a receiver scope | None |
| Access Token Issuance (RAS) | The RAS MAY include instance context only for the instance it validated at redemption; the instance draft is then its own consuming profile (§7.5). It MUST NOT copy or remap context from the ID-JAG or WAG. Instance context is not an actor and replaces nothing | +1 MAY, +1 MUST NOT |
| Token Validation (API) | Applies INSTANCE §7.5, and MUST NOT treat instance context as satisfying the actor gate or the agent's own permissions. Attribution needs INSTANCE's sender constraint | +1 MUST NOT |
| Effects table, Privacy | A "Suspend one client instance" row, and per-receiver and per-consumer scoping of instance identifiers | None |
| Scope, excluded compositions, references | Endorsement and RAS-validated instance context move into scope. Only grant-carried or cross-domain instance context stays excluded. INSTANCE and ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT become normative datatracker references | None |

## SCIM OAuth client management

- `client_attesters` is added to the OAuthClient metadata extension. It is a multi-valued complex attribute of `{issuer, jwks_uri}` objects, the one exception to string-array metadata, with a schema entry and the extension listing.
- The Service Provider MUST accept a value only from a provisioning client authorized to set endorsements for that client (ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT §2.2), including when a request replaces or removes the attribute. Authority to manage the registration alone does not suffice (+1 MUST).
- Rejection uses this draft's SCIM errors, not §2.2's OAuth `invalid_client_metadata` or keep-the-previous-value options (b3b1ca2):
  - `403` for an unauthorized change;
  - `400` with `invalidValue` for a malformed endorsement or one the policy does not accept.

  The request fails and the stored resource is unchanged.
- CIMD resources carry no `client_attesters`; their endorsements come from the document.

## Coordination and README

- COORDINATION.md is assessed against both -00 drafts. It adds a note with two items for the instance draft:
  - its Appendix A.3 example names the issuing authorization server as `act.iss`, but under governed actor preservation the RAS keeps the IdP's issuer;
  - carrying instance context in the grant would need this profile to become a consuming profile under INSTANCE §7.4.
- The README says instances and endorsements compose as evidence beside the governed agent.

## Not included, deliberately

- Instances as governed sub-principals, or per-instance authorization.
- Instance context carried in the ID-JAG or WAG and preserved across domains.
- Instance lifecycle over SCIM or Shared Signals.

Both edited drafts build clean. The core draft goes from 92 to 93 pages, and the SCIM schema JSON parses.

pulls.title: Allow managed-installation bindings instead of banning instance resolution
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
PR #13 turned deferred instance-based resolution into a ban: a client instance identifier "MUST NOT select or change the Agent Principal". That forecloses a case the AAuth Agent Provider design sketch relies on ([gist](https://gist.github.com/mcguinness/234b6abeecc4f01693f026d00c1b617b)): an enterprise approving and retiring particular managed installations behind one shared OAuth client.

At installation granularity, under the instance draft's continuity rules (§6), an attested installation is a qualified workload identity, like a SPIFFE ID. The governance-boundary rules already give independently governed actors separate principals, even behind one client. The real risk is an instance implicitly picking or switching the agent, and an exact, approved Identity Binding closes it, as it does for every other input.

## Changes

| Where | Rule | Keywords |
|---|---|---|
| Identity Binding | An identifier of one execution (process, replica, or container) MUST NOT select or change the Agent Principal. A client instance identifier MUST NOT do so except through the managed-installation binding, and MUST NOT satisfy a Client Association | +2 MUST NOT |
| Client Attestation input: new "Managed installation" rule | Where agents share one OAuth client, an attestation carrying `client_instance_id` MAY resolve the agent. The rest of the rule is listed below | +1 MAY, +1 MUST, +3 MUST NOT |
| Input table, effects table | The Client Attestation row adds the IdP receiver scope and `client_instance_id` for a managed installation. Suspending an instance leaves "the agent's other bindings and instances" running | None |
| COORDINATION.md, README | Instances resolve an agent only through an exact, approved installation binding | None |
| SCIM agent management (04616ac) | `AgentIdentityBinding` gains optional, immutable `clientInstanceId` and `receiverScope`, permitted only for `client-attestation` and required together. The Service Provider MUST reject a binding whose level differs from the level configured for that attester and client. Both join the uniqueness key, so two installations behind one client no longer collide | +2 MUST |

The rest of the managed-installation rule:
- The IdP MUST accept the attestation only from an attester configured for installation granularity, under INSTANCE §6.
- The binding names the exact attester, client (`sub`), IdP receiver scope, and `client_instance_id`.
- Trusted configuration selects client-level or installation-level resolution. Attestation claims MUST NOT select the level, and a failed match MUST NOT fall back to the other level.
- A new enrollment needs its own approved binding. The IdP MUST NOT infer continuity across identifiers or attesters.

## Unchanged

- Identifiers of individual executions (pods, replicas) never resolve an agent, so elastic workloads stay on workload identity.
- Instance context in tokens is still limited to the instance the RAS validated.
- Endorsements still never create bindings.

Review fixes:
- SCIM representation of installation bindings (04616ac).
- A split COORDINATION.md table row (7483bb4).

Both drafts build clean, and the SCIM schema JSON parses. The gist marks this binding "pending merge". After this merges, I'll re-pin the gist to the merge commit.

pulls.title: Grant-level replay, narrower platform-JWT requirement, WAG boundary, and negative tests
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies a review of the September 28 draft. The review's central question: does the document make independent implementations agree on what an issued grant commits the IdP to, what the RAS must verify, and what the API can rely on? Each commit is one recommendation. ## Changes | Commit | Change | Keywords | |---|---|---| | 86fe4d3 | **Grant replay keyed on the grant's own binding.** Single use was inherited only through Actor Profile §4.2, which applies to grants carrying `act` and switches off whenever the token endpoint requires DPoP or mutual TLS. An unbound grant redeemed with an access-token DPoP proof was therefore exempt, and an unbound WAG had no replay rule at all. Common Grant Validation now states that for a grant without an enforced grant-level sender constraint, the RAS MUST reject a reused (`iss`, `jti`). A proof used only for client authentication or access-token binding does not count. The RAS MAY accept a bound grant again under explicit policy, with a fresh matching proof each time. This narrows ID-JAG §4.4.3 re-submission for unbound grants and settles WAG-01 §8's open replay question. Also updated: a redemption error row, the base-spec table, the renewal row, Security (single use limits a stolen unbound grant to one redemption, not zero), and COORDINATION.md | +1 MUST, +1 MAY | | d5a546c | **Platform JWT only for a generic shared-client claim.** Previously, supporting any other input required the platform JWT. Now claiming an input requires only that input's rules. An implementation claiming generic shared-client interoperability MUST support the platform JWT, and conformance claims state whether they make that claim | Two conditional MUSTs become one | | c89a314 | **WAG compatibility boundary.** This document specifies a governed composition of WAG that generic WAG support does not imply. It defines the complete wire contract, so WAG stays informative, and the composition remains subject to alignment. A table lists each difference from WAG-01: issuer, client authentication and `client_id`, grant binding, `typ`, replay, `resource`, unseen agents, refresh | None | | 039d2c3 | **Applicability portability.** Conformance alone gives no portable discriminator for every mixed-token deployment. A configuration example is added, and one registration and one audience serving several populations needs a bilateral contract | None | | 097f762 | **Early motivation and a bounded promise.** A four-sentence shared-client scenario is added to the Service Provider Contract. "Disable everywhere" is qualified: this profile establishes what disablement acts on, and propagation depends on the selected lifecycle mechanism | None | | d856720 | **Negative tests.** The rejection table becomes "Negative test cases" and gains four cases:
• an unbound grant re-redeemed with another key;
• a missing `act` does not make a token self-acting;
• no token reuse across agents behind a shared client;
• no resolution retry after a platform JWT fails | None | | 2b04323 | The WAG table describes WAG-01's `resource` level in prose, not as a BCP 14 keyword | None | | 54fb370 | Both redemption checklists name the replay step, and negative tests add an unbound WAG presented twice | None | ## Net - **Keywords:** MUST count unchanged; MAY +1. - **Size:** 93 → 95 pages, 20,304 → 20,958 words. The WAG table and the new test rows account for most of the growth. - **Build:** clean. ## Related - Actor Profile: mcguinness/draft-mcguinness-oauth-actor-profile#5 proposes the same grant-level condition for its §4.2 replay rule. - Not adopted from the review: moving the optional inputs into a separate bindings document, a structural lever still open.

pulls.title: Govern platform-hosted agents without putting the IdP on the runtime path
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Some platforms host agents for a customer that use only the platform's own tools and resources, for example a data platform's first-party agents. The IdP issues those agents nothing and may not know they exist. The platform must keep operating without the IdP, but the enterprise wants one inventory, one governance decision, and centralized monitoring for them, and may later need them to reach third-party resources.

The family didn't address this. Every companion assumed the IdP was on the runtime path:
- Agent management said "the IdP remains the authority for the Agent Principal", and its scope was delegated ID-JAG issuance.
- Lifecycle ran one way, IdP → resource domain, and enforced only at an OAuth RAS.
- Nothing carried events from the platform to the IdP.

Most of the machinery already existed. Agents need no binding. Lifecycle's effective eligibility is already an AND of IdP state and a Local Suspension, and transport failure is already not deletion. This PR states the pattern and adds the missing direction.

## Changes

| Draft | Change | Keywords |
|---|---|---|
| SCIM agent management (220f7e9) | New **Platform-Hosted Agents** section. The connector registers each hosted agent as an Agent with no binding or association, so it gets no grant. It sets `externalId` to the platform's identifier and supplies `owners` and descriptive attributes, and the platform keeps the returned qualified identifier as its correlation. The IdP decides `active`: registration or description authority MUST NOT include setting `active: true` on an Agent the IdP disabled. Deleting the agent deletes the Agent, and its identity is not reused. IdP policy MAY create registered Agents inactive until approved, which makes activation, not operation, depend on the IdP. To federate later, an administrator adds a binding and association to the same Agent | +1 MUST NOT, +1 MAY |
| Lifecycle (23b5be8) | New **Platform-Hosted Agents** section, described below. New **Platform Signals to the IdP**, also below. Scope, Receiver definition, and conformance name the platform case | +3 MUST, +1 SHOULD, +2 MAY |
| README (1f31616) | A **Platform-hosted agents** section summarizing the pattern | None |

**Lifecycle, Platform-Hosted Agents:**
- The platform is the Receiver for its registered agents, and its own resources are the resource domain.
- Correlation is the identifier registration returned.
- The platform gets `active` from IdP provisioning, or by retrieving its registered Agent on a change notice or during reconciliation.
- On `active: false`, it MUST deny new authorization and revoke the agent's existing authorization in its own system. Its own suspension is a Local Suspension the IdP cannot clear.
- **The IdP is not on the platform's runtime path:** an unreachable IdP neither disables nor re-enables agents. The existing revalidation policy is the optional staleness bound.
- Audit records and telemetry SHOULD carry the qualified identifier as the join key; no log format is defined.

**Lifecycle, Platform Signals to the IdP:**
- The platform MAY transmit CAEP `credential-change`, `session-revoked`, and `risk-level-change` for agents its connector registered, identified with an `iss_sub` subject (RFC 9493 §3.2.3).
- Stream configuration MUST establish that scope, and the IdP MUST reject events about other agents.
- Events inform policy; they don't change administrative state.
- The IdP MAY send `risk-level-change` back to the platform; it is not a disablement.

## Defaults chosen (author decisions)

- **Push registration:** the platform registers its agents at the IdP. IdP discovery by reading a platform's inventory is noted as outside the profile.
- **IdP disablement binds the platform:** once the platform applies `active: false`, it MUST deny and revoke.
- **Approval before activation is optional IdP policy.** It is not the default, because the platform must operate independently. When used, an Agent registered inactive is denied like any inactive Agent until approved; there is no separate approval state (addc110, from review).

## Out of scope, unchanged

- Log and telemetry formats.
- Risk engines and posture models.

The drafts supply the correlation key and the control and event channels. The README already places telemetry outside this architecture.

Both drafts build clean. The lifecycle draft's 29 over-long lines predate this PR and are left as they were.

pulls.title: Platform-hosted agent walkthrough, and WISE for workload signals
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Adds an end-to-end scenario for a first-party agent on a platform, using the pattern merged in #16. It also adopts the OpenID Shared Signals WG's WISE profile ([draft 03](https://openid.github.io/ssf-wise-profile/)) for workload signals, with CAEP kept for sessions and IdP risk.

## Walkthrough (bf7ae7f, 5c3954c)

A new lifecycle appendix, **Platform-Hosted Agent Walkthrough**, follows one data-platform agent: `agt-31`, registered with workload identifier `wimse://dataplatform.example/agents/agt-31` and assigned `agent-58` at the IdP.

1. **Configure:**
   - The connector may register and describe agents. It cannot create bindings or associations, or enable an Agent the IdP disabled.
   - IdP → platform: SCIM change notices and CAEP `risk-level-change`.
   - Platform → IdP: WISE credential and posture events and CAEP `session-revoked`.
   - No revalidation bound is set.
2. **Register (14:00):**
   - A SCIM POST with `owners`, and the workload URI as `externalId`.
   - The IdP returns `agent-58`. With no binding, the agent gets no grant.
   - The approval-first variant is described.
3. **Operate:** platform-native authorization with no IdP call. An illustrative audit record carries both identifiers.
4. **Credential change (14:20):** WISE `credential-rotated` (`wic`) with an RFC 9493 `aliases` subject naming the Agent Principal (`iss_sub`) and the workload (`uri`).
5. **Anomaly (14:25):** WISE `anomalous-behavior-detected`, which is advisory.
6. **Risk (14:30):** the IdP's analysis sends CAEP `risk-level-change` (HIGH). The platform restricts the agent to read-only; this is not a disablement.
7. **Disable (14:31):**
   - SCIM change notice, then retrieval.
   - The platform denies new authorization, revokes sessions, and reports `session-revoked` back.
   - The case where the IdP is unreachable is shown.
8. **Re-enable (15:00):** revoked sessions stay revoked, and a Local Suspension isn't cleared.
9. **Third-party access, with explicit delegation (from review):**
   - Alice, who is not the owner, delegates to the agent.
   - The platform presents her ID Token as `subject_token` and its JWT as `actor_token`. The ID-JAG has Alice in `sub` and `agent-58` in `act`.
   - `owners` do not establish delegation.
   - Self-acting access would instead need Agent Authorization and a WAG.
10. **Retire (16:00):** DELETE at the IdP. The identifier is never reused.

## Signals

| Commit | Change | Keywords |
|---|---|---|
| d3ea619, 099e4ca | CAEP defines no agent `principal`, so stream configuration MUST fix it. After the WISE change, this applies only to the IdP's `risk-level-change` | +1 MUST |
| 099e4ca | **Platform Signals to the IdP use WISE** for credential and posture events, with CAEP `session-revoked` for sessions. The subject is `aliases` (`iss_sub` plus the WISE `uri` the platform registered), and the IdP MUST correlate both with the same Agent or reject the event. A platform's own WISE workload-disabled, -enabled, or -purged reports local control, not IdP `active`. **SCIM Reconciliation Triggers:** WISE `workload-disabled` and `-purged` MAY cause a provisional Local Suspension. WISE `workload-enabled` and `-restored` trigger retrieval and MUST NOT activate directly, which keeps the notice-then-retrieve safety property. The WISE reference moves from an old personal repository (informative) to WG draft 03 (normative) | +1 MUST, +1 MUST NOT, +1 MAY |
| 3294c96 | **Core:** an IdP that accepts WISE events from a credential authority MUST stop resolving through credentials that `credential-revoked` or `-compromised` identifies, trust material that `trust-anchor-revoked` identifies, and trust domains that `trust-domain-federation-revoked` names. Disabling a binding or the agent in response stays IdP policy | +1 MUST |
| ee4f92b | Agent management: a platform that sends WISE events uses their workload URI as `externalId`. README: direct link to the walkthrough (from review), and the signals bullet names WISE and CAEP | None |
| e2a0f92 | COORDINATION.md records the WISE `aliases` subject ask, the enabled-event asymmetry, the missing agent principal value, and moving the reference to openid.net once published | None |

## Notes

- WISE is a working-group draft, cited at its editor's copy because draft 03 is not yet on openid.net. Its normative use is limited to deployments that enable these signals.
- Builds are clean, and all walkthrough JSON parses. The core draft goes from 95 to 97 pages: the rule and its reference add 21 lines, which shift page breaks.
